AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To describe parents' use of nonpharmacologic methods to manage infant procedural pain in the NICU and determine the demographic factors related to such use.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A cross-sectional and descriptive study design.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Level III and Level II NICUs (seven units) of four University Hospitals in Finland.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Parents (N = 178) whose infants were treated in Finnish NICUs.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Parents were asked to respond to a structured questionnaire during their infants' hospitalizations. We analyzed the data using the nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis one-way analysis of variance and Mann-Whitney U test.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Most parents reported that they used physical methods, such as touching, holding, and positioning, nearly always/always (86%, 76%, and 55%, respectively). However, less commonly used strategies included recorded music (2%), breastfeeding (2%), non-nutritive sucking, and oral sucrose (6%). Many characteristics of the infants, such as their gestational ages and their conditions, were significantly related to the implementation of nonpharmacologic methods.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: There is a clear need to extend parents' use of nonpharmacologic methods to manage their infants' procedural pain in the NICU. Because many methods were not considered as pain-relieving strategies, it is important to increase knowledge about the effectiveness of these interventions among parents and nurses.

Article.ArticleTitle: Parents' Use of Nonpharmacologic Methods to Manage Procedural Pain in Infants.

Journal.Title: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
